name: Māori sky
summary: The seafaring figures of New Zealand’s indigenous people: canoes, sails and anchor ropes in the sky, used for navigation and to mark planting time.

001.name: Taki-o-Autahi
001.description: The Southern Cross; its other Māori name is Mahutonga. Not visible from Hungary.

002.name: The Rope of Tama-rereti’s Canoe
002.description: The two bright stars of Centaurus, the “Pointers” that point towards the Southern Cross: the rope of the canoe. Not visible from Hungary.

003.name: Tau-toro
003.description: The three stars of Orion’s Belt.

004.name: Tama-rereti’s Great Canoe
004.description: The curving tail of Scorpius: Tama-rereti’s long canoe. From Hungary it is visible only low, near the southern horizon.

005.name: Matakarehu
005.description: The V-shaped Hyades that form the head of Taurus, and the reddish Aldebaran (in Māori, Taumatakuku).

006.name: The Sail of Tainui
006.description: A figure with no European counterpart: a seafaring double canoe. Orion’s Belt is the keel, the Hyades the claw-shaped sail, and the Pleiades (in Māori, Matariki) the prow. Tainui is one of the legendary migration canoes of the Māori.
